summary: Three well-made passages (830 / 826 / 825 words): the history of the circus, packaging grown from fungus, and the spacing effect in learning. Difficulty rises properly, and passage 3 is close to real IELTS. All answer keys are correct. Two TRUE/FALSE/NOT GIVEN questions were out of passage order and have been swapped. Eight broken paraphrase pairs were fixed and pairs were added, so 39 of 40 questions now have one.
strengths: Full IELTS question mix: sentence completion, TFNG, matching information, summary completion, matching people with a spare name, MCQ, YNNG and sentence endings.

Passage 3 argues a real case (massed vs spaced practice, 'desirable difficulties', the fluency illusion) with C1 vocabulary, and its MCQ distractors reverse what the passage says (meaningless syllables, the spacing finding ignored for decades).
NOT GIVEN items are truly unaddressed (Astley's fortune, Cirque du Soleil's profits, software vs card boxes), and FALSE/NO items are clearly contradicted.
Most completion prompts paraphrase the passage ('stay upright' / 'keep his feet', 'special' / 'dedicated', 'in diameter' / 'across').

issues.problem: TFNG questions 8 and 9 were out of passage order: Q8 (the word 'circus', paragraph 4) came before Q9 (Astley's European amphitheatres, end of paragraph 3).
issues.change: Reordered: Q8 is now 'Astley made a large fortune from his European amphitheatres.' (NOT GIVEN) and Q9 is now 'Astley was the first person to use the word 'circus'...' (FALSE). Numbers and types kept; explanations and evidence moved with the statements. Answer pattern is now T, NG, F, T, F, T, NG (no runs of three).

issues.problem: Eight pairs used question wording the student never sees: Q11 'fewer people', Q12 'without animals', Q19 'waste' (as the question side), Q23 'factory', Q27 'rapidly lost', Q30 'by feeling', Q35 'no one ideal'; Q26's text side 'not identical' is not in the passage.
issues.change: Q11 ['audiences', 'people to attend circus performances']; Q12 ['no animals of any kind', 'without any animal acts']; Q19 ['Production starts with', 'Production begins with']; Q23 ['The gap narrows', 'extra cost of grown packaging will shrink']; Q26 ['no two batches are ever quite identical', 'Differences between batches']; Q27 ['newly learned material fades most quickly', 'how rapidly new learning is lost']; Q30 ['we judge our own learning', 'learners judge progress']; Q35 ['The best gap', 'one ideal interval'].

issues.problem: Several valid pairs were single words that taught little (Q20 'finished'/'final', Q22 'garden'/'ordinary', Q25 'polystyrene'/'plastic foam', Q28 'evidence of mastery'/'false sense', Q32 'respectable performance'/'benefit', Q38 'builds'/'strengthens').
issues.change: Replaced with the phrase a student needs to find: Q20 ['shaped like the finished product', 'the shape of the final product'], Q22 ['a mycelium block disappears', 'a buried block breaks down'], Q25 ['for cushioning fragile goods', 'protects delicate goods'], Q28 ['the smoothness is misread', 'a false sense of how much they have mastered'], Q32 ['tomorrow morning's test', 'a test the following day'], Q38 ['builds stronger memories', 'strengthens memory']. New pairs added for Q4, Q8, Q9, Q14, Q18, Q21, Q29, Q33, Q34.

issues.problem: Q2 'The traditional circus ring is about thirteen ______ in diameter' gives the number away and only asks for the unit 'metres', so it is almost free.
issues.change: Test a real idea instead, e.g. 'Astley's ring was wide enough for a comfortable ______' (answer: canter), or 'A ring of this size allowed every ______ to be close to the action' (answer: seat).

issues.problem: The passage 2 summary repeats the passage's words around two gaps ('agricultural {{19}}', 'dried using {{21}}'), so these are easy to find by scanning.
issues.change: Paraphrase the summary, e.g. 'Production begins with farm {{19}}' and 'The piece is then dried by applying {{21}}'.

issues.problem: Q13 (Cirque du Soleil 'the most profitable circus company in history') has no pair: the passage has no phrase that means the same; it only mentions audiences in the millions.
issues.change: None needed; left without a pair.
